title: The great forty
hookLine: right view leads, and the other factors follow
last: A MOUNTAIN THAT SEEMED TO SWALLOW THEM.

lines: A PERFECT GPS, A WRONG ADDRESS.
cards: A GPS can be perfect in every other way: smooth voice, live traffic, a lovely map. But if the destination you typed in is wrong, every turn it gives is a good turn toward the wrong place.
The eightfold path has eight parts, and it's easy to picture them like the spokes of a wheel, all equal. The hundred and seventeenth discourse, called the Great Forty, says something more specific.
Of the eight, one goes first.

teach.b: The discourse starts with noble right concentration: a still mind, supported by the other seven factors, right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort and mindfulness.
Then the Buddha says it plainly, factor after factor: right view comes first. How?
You understand wrong view as wrong view, and right view as right view. That understanding is itself your right view.
He does the same with each factor: you know wrong intention as wrong, and right intention as right: that's right view.

And around each factor three things keep circling: right view, which sees it clearly; right effort, which works to drop the wrong and build the right; and right mindfulness, which remembers to keep at it.

The text also splits right view in two. There's the ordinary kind, believing that giving matters and actions have results, which leads to good births. And there's the noble kind, wisdom itself, on the way to freedom.
Then the count. For someone fully awake, the eight factors grow to ten: right knowledge and right release are added. Ten right factors, and ten wrong ones.
Each wrong one is a source of many harmful things, each right one a source of many good things.

teach.h: TWENTY AND TWENTY: THE GREAT FORTY
teach.b: Twenty on the side of the wholesome, twenty on the side of the unwholesome. That's the great forty.
And at the front of all forty, in the text's telling, stands view: what you think is real, and what you think matters.

how: The eightfold path is often taught as three trainings of wisdom, virtue and concentration, and some Theravada teachers draw on MN 117 to explain why right view is placed first.

o: the view from the top after long meditation
holding the correct opinion in every argument
right view: seeing what's real and what matters

games.q: the great forty: tap the pairs.
p: the two added for the fully awake

s: MN 117 says all eight factors come first equally
it says right view comes first, again and again.
the discourse speaks of two kinds of right view
an ordinary kind, that actions have results, and a noble kind that is wisdom itself.
the forty are forty different meditation methods
they are ten right and ten wrong factors, each a source of many good or harmful things: twenty and twenty.

games.q: you know wrong speech as wrong speech, and right speech as right speech. in MN 117, what is that knowing called?
games.why: the knowing itself is right view. then right effort and right mindfulness work alongside it on speech.

practice: Pick one thing ahead of you, a meeting, a call, a chore, and before thinking how to do it, ask what you believe it's for: winning, being liked, helping, or just getting it over with.
Let the honest answer show up, and if you like, choose the view you'd want leading and let the breath carry it.

wordCard.voice: Samma ditthi. Right view, the first factor of the path: in the Buddha's teaching here, it comes first among the great forty, with effort and mindfulness circling every step.

orig.note: Pali samma ditthi: right view, the first factor of the path.

carryVoice: Your line: view leads. Where you think you're going shapes every turn. See you tomorrow.
